newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian premier escapes assassination attempt.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian premier escapes assassination attempt.

text.p: fired at a car carrying Cambodian co-Prime Minister Hun Sen in an apparent assassination attempt, officials in the premier's office said on Thursday.
Hun Sen was not hurt, but a motorcyle escort rider was slightly wounded as the premier travelled through Phnom Penh on Wednesday evening, they said.
The gunman escaped, the officials said.
A senior official in Hun Sen's security unit said the premier was the target of the attack.
"Of course, the shooter wanted to kill the Second Prime Minister," security officer Tarn Seray told Reuters.
Interior Ministry spokesman Sok Phal said at least one shot was fired at Hun Sen's car from a rifle equipped with a silencer as he drove through central Phnom Penh.
"As the car was travelling so fast, the bullet hit the motorcyle escort just behind it," Sok Phal told Reuters.
The escort rider was hit in the head but was not seriously wounded, police said.

Hun Sen, currently locked in a bitter power struggle with his coalition partner, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, told reporters earlier this month that there had been several attempts on his life, or plots to kill him, in recent years.
Hun Sen and Ranariddh have been waging a war of words for months over a series of disagreements including power-sharing in their coalition government.

Earlier this week, troops loyal to the two premiers confronted each other in a tense face-off as their commanders argued over an arms shipment that Hun Sen's party said Ranariddh was trying to import illegally. The disagreement was finally settled peacefully.
